disposition_reason: Fourteen elements including Cd, Cr, Ni, Co, Ba, Mo and Al were measured by ICP-OES in 47 gluten-free rice-based pastas and flours and gluten-containing wheat pastas from Las Vegas markets; Table 1 prints each sample and Table 2 group statistics.

study.design: Market survey of 42 gluten-free (31 US-made, 11 Asian imports) and 5 gluten-containing products
study.origin: manufactured in the US (36) or imported from Asia (11); agricultural source of the plant material unknown
study.method: Hot aqua regia digestion (USEPA 3050B), ICP-OES (USEPA 6010B), triplicate
study.lod_text: IDL Al 5, Ba 2, Ca 5, Cd 2, Co 2, Cr 2, Cu 2, Fe 3, Mg 5, Mn 3, Mo 3, Ni 3, Ti 3, Zn 5; LOQ 3x IDL (Table 2, units as printed)
study.qa: Certified reference sample from a USEPA-certified supplier within certified windows; RSD < 20% for triplicates; recoveries not reported

controls.control: gluten-free rice-based vs gluten-containing wheat pasta
controls.outcome: Cd mean 260 µg/kg wheat pasta vs 270 (US) and 333 (Asian) µg/kg gluten-free; Cr 1700 vs 241 and 581 µg/kg; Ni 5138 vs 1221 and 2144 µg/kg

unresolved: Lead and arsenic were not measured.
Table 1 rows 37 (Co) and 40 (Fe) have blank cells, not '-'; no finding recorded.
Per-sample values for Ca, Cu, Fe, Mg, Ti and Zn are in sample_values.
Detection-limit units in Table 2 are not stated; values look like µg/L in solution.
'r' (rice products) is the paper's label; corn-based products are mentioned in Methods but not separated.
